reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The triangle represents one tile in the shape of a triangle.

[Image: An equilateral triangle labeled "tile"]

How many tiles will it take to cover the figure below?

[Image: A polygon drawn on an isometric dot grid]

Number of tiles: ____

Use the figure above to show how you worked out your answer.

descriptors: 14. Figure is correctly partitioned.
14. Partition includes errors.
14. Partition is not shown.
The figure is correctly partitioned. Triangles are miscounted. (Count does not equal 14.)
Neither partition nor number of triangles is correct.
Other incorrect.

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top is an equilateral triangle with dots at each of its three vertices, labeled "tile" to the right of its right edge.

Below is an irregular polygon drawn on an isometric (triangular) dot grid, with dots marking vertices along its boundary and in its interior:
- Top edge: a horizontal segment 3 units long, with 4 dots evenly spaced (including endpoints).
- Left boundary: from the top-left dot, a line goes down and right by 1 unit to an indented vertex dot; from there, a line goes down and left by 1 unit to the bottom-left corner dot.
- Bottom edge: a horizontal segment 4 units long, with 5 dots evenly spaced (including endpoints).
- Right boundary: from the top-right dot, a line goes down and right by 1 unit to a vertex dot at the middle horizontal level; from that dot, a horizontal line extends right by 1 unit to another vertex dot; from that dot, a line goes down and left by 1 unit to the bottom-right corner dot.
- Interior: 2 dots are spaced along the middle horizontal level between the left indented vertex and the right boundary.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Sam said that 1/3 of a pie is less than 1/4 of the same pie.

Is Sam correct? ____

Use the circles below to show why this is so.

[Image: Two circles]

Shade in 1/3 of this circle

Shade in 1/4 of this circle

descriptors: NO. Both circles are correctly partitioned.
NO. No partitioning is shown.
NO. Only one of the circles correctly partitioned.
NO. Other incorrect ways of partitioning.
YES, or there is no conclusion stated. Both circles are correctly partitioned.
Other partial.
YES. No partitioning is shown.
YES. The part representing 1/3 is made consistently smaller than the part representing 1/4.
YES. Other responses where one or both of the circles partitioned into 3 and/or 4 parts.
Other incorrect.

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: The partition of circles has priority over shading. This is reflected in the scoring guide below.
reference_items.figure_description: Two identical, empty circles are shown side by side. Below the left circle is the text "Shade in 1/3 of this circle" with 1/3 written as a vertical fraction. Below the right circle is the text "Shade in 1/4 of this circle" with 1/4 written as a vertical fraction.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
